 * bayestar.multiorder.fits,0, an initial localization generated by BAYESTAR [4], distributed via GCN and SCiMMA notices about 28 seconds after the candidate event time.
 * bayestar.multiorder.fits,1, an initial localization generated by BAYESTAR [4], distributed via GCN and SCiMMA notices about 5 minutes after the candidate event time.
 * bayestar.multiorder.fits,2, an initial localization generated by BAYESTAR [4], distributed via GCN and SCiMMA notices about 2 days after the candidate event time.
The preferred sky map at this time is bayestar.multiorder.fits,2.

answer.text: The GCN notice stream lists a first position at 2025-08-18 01:20:35 UTC · LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (igwn.gwalert) · RA 99.027°, Dec −59.109°, while later notices give RA 242.314°, Dec +37.169° and then RA 242.754°, Dec +37.638° on 2025-08-20.

Circular 41437 reports that three sky maps are available at this time, distributed about 28 seconds, 5 minutes, and 2 days after the event, and that the preferred sky map at this time is bayestar.multiorder.fits,2, whose 90% credible region is 786 deg2.
Circular 41440 then reports a new map, Bilby.offline0.multiorder.fits,0, with a 90% credible region of 949 deg2.
The circulars do not state a direct comparison between the 786 deg2 and 949 deg2 regions, and they come from different map types, so the reason for the difference is not documented.
